cells.tense: The whole cycle just landed, and you're holding it in your hands, not already reaching for the next thing.
cells.ask: Offer one piece of what you've come to see to someone nearby, exactly as large as it feels today.
cells.core:
You're not running the past in a loop and not rehearsing a future — the whole arc of feeling you've lived through is here, and you can look across it.
That's this working well: you don't pretend the fog isn't there, and you don't turn it into a map too early. You let the shape finish itself, and it did. What's available now is more of this knowing said out loud, to someone who gets it, before it hardens into a lesson. Plenty of people file an experience away before it's done. You let it be whole first, and that's worth spending.

cells.tense: You're already feeling the completion that hasn't happened yet and trying to act like it has.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you might do this week and run it as is — one move, no rehearsal, no perfecting.
cells.core:
One step on the light you've got, and the next patch shows up on its own — that's the whole trick of moving through uncertainty, and most of the time you already do it without thinking. You don't need to see the end to keep walking.
What's happening now runs the other way. You reach for the finish before the ground is under it, running every possible ending at once, and when the light is dim the urge to be done gets strongest. The fog doesn't clear because you hurry it. A seed is not a proof; one move you actually make teaches you more than a forecast of how it goes.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that isn't in front of you anymore.
cells.ask: Say out loud something you honestly noticed yesterday — no preface, just it.
cells.core:
When this is live, a fresh turn toward what's next shows up without being forced — you move on a patch of light, and the next one arrives, and you don't need the whole route to take it.
That reach has gone quiet. A pull keeps you back at something you already passed, and feelings and insight are still around while the unforced move toward the next thing isn't. Enough light for one step is enough. The fog doesn't have to lift first and the past doesn't have to be settled. The reach just needs room to happen.

cells.tense: The arc is already being held, and you're describing it as if it were still open.
cells.ask: Name one thing you actually see, to someone who'll simply receive it — one sentence, stated, not debated.
cells.core:
Something plain lands and doesn't need arguing for, because it already fits what you see — that's how knowing works at its clearest, and you get there more often than you'd claim.
Some of that is steering through this uncertainty right now, quietly, with no credit coming back to you. Meanwhile the situation gets talked about as if it were still up in the air. Sitting in that isn't confusion so much as having to stand behind a thing you hadn't said. It doesn't need anyone's vote. It needs the sentence.
